title: Australia Postcodes by State & Suburb
description: Browse Australia Postcodes by State & Suburb — postcode ranges for NSW, Victoria, Queensland and every state and territory. Free reference.
summary_sentence: For example, Sydney's 2000, Melbourne's 3000 and Perth's 6000 show the system's logic at a glance: in most states the thousands digit is the state's signature.
quick_answer: Australia Postcodes by State & Suburb organises Australian postcodes the way Australia Post allocates them — by state and territory, then by suburb. Pick a state and browse its ranges: the 2xxx block is New South Wales, 3xxx Victoria, 4xxx Queensland, and so on across the national postcode map.

body.t: A postcode that starts with 7 cannot be in Victoria — the state blocks make a first-pass sanity check for Australian address data before any lookup runs.
Service areas in Australia are quoted by postcode ranges. The state blocks turn a coverage promise ('all of metro Sydney') into an enumerable list.
Suburb-postcode mismatches in a CRM surface fastest when the state's whole range is in front of you — browse the block and the strangers stand out.

The 2000 (Sydney CBD) and 3000 (Melbourne CBD) centroids sit about 713 km apart — the two biggest postcode blocks' capitals, an overnight drive apart. The blocks' capitals define most Australians' sense of the system.
Darwin is 0800, in the Northern Territory's 0xxx block — always write the zero. Dropping it (800) breaks forms, sorts and lookups, the most common Australian postcode bug in imported data.

popular_table.intro: Australia Post's allocation — the thousands digit does most of the work.
popular_table.note: Ranges are the allocation blocks in general use; individual postcodes are created, retired and shared by suburbs over time, and a handful of codes serve large mail users. Australia Post's own lookup is the authority for a specific address.

faq: Why do some postcodes serve many suburbs?
A postcode is a mail-sorting area, not a suburb boundary — dense city centres stack many suburbs into one code, while rural codes spread across a district. Suburb and postcode are cousins, not twins.
Can a suburb have several postcodes?
Yes — large suburbs split across codes, and new developments redraw the map. The browse shows the common allocations; an exact address belongs to Australia Post's finder.
What about PO Box and large-user postcodes?
Some codes exist only for post office boxes or single large recipients and never appear on a street map. Their absence from suburb lists is correct behaviour.
Christmas Island (6798), Cocos (6799) and Norfolk Island (2899) sit inside the state blocks' leftovers — the ranges table's fine print, findable in their host blocks.
Postcode allocations change as Australia Post creates and retires codes. Treat this browse as the reference map of the system; verify a critical address at the source.
Postcodes versus time zones or area codes?
No relation — telephone area codes (02, 03, 07, 08) roughly echo states by historical accident of the same federation, but the systems are independent.
Why does NSW include 2620 near Canberra?
Geography ignores the territory border — a few NSW postcodes wrap around the ACT. The table notes the shared corner rather than hiding it.
